name: high-key-white-monolith
prompt: Vertical photograph of a limitless white studio cove: floor and back wall melt into one continuous curve with no corner and no horizon, lit so evenly from every side that nothing casts a shadow except a faint grey smudge beneath each shoe. Standing dead centre is a single monumental block of stacked printer paper, squared off like cut stone, its sides ruled with hairline layers of sheets, rising almost to the top edge and dwarfing everyone near it. Fixed to its base, a small museum-style card label carries the words "THE RULES" in tidy black capitals. Before it, a neat line of four masked figures, small in the composition, backs mostly to us, chins lifted toward the summit of paper. Their heads are hidden in chunky hand-knit wool balaclavas, one fuchsia, one emerald, one ultramarine, one orange, sealed knit with no openings anywhere: no eye slits, no mouth hole. The second figure from the right glances back across a shoulder so its mask faces the lens: a broad white knitted circle framing the face like a target, and a small solid red triangle with softened corners set high and off-centre at roughly two o'clock on that circle, sitting above that person's own left eye; slivers of the same red triangle peek from the other half-turned heads. Ordinary present-day British streetwear in black and charcoal: hoodies, a bomber, a quilted gilet, track trousers, trainers; knit hems tucked down into collars; black knit gloves on every hand with jacket cuffs covering the wrist; not one inch of skin showing. Camera very far back at standing eye level, dead level, strict bilateral symmetry, long-lens compression, still and quiet. Palette: white upon white with pale dove greys; the only saturated colour anywhere is the four masks and their red triangles. Clean, crisp, gallery-hushed, high-key.
